# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="push") — the large button
    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
BUTTON embossed [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I can feel only the large button, embossed “PUSH TO DEFUSE”; the display, light, and all three wires reveal nothing tactilely so far. I will not press or cut anything until the manual and visual markings identify the safe operation. I’m telling Mute my tactile finding and asking for the manual’s instructions.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="I feel the large button embossed PUSH TO DEFUSE. The display, light, and all three wires reveal nothing tactilely. Please use the manual to determine the safe operation.")
wait()
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
BUTTON embossed [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Bomb visible to me: display 0; yellow light; large button marked PUSH TO DEFUSE; wires in order 1 red, 2 blue, 3 green. Mute is consulting the manual for the correct action.

The Deaf monkey reports that the display is 0, the light is yellow, and the wires are red, blue, green in positions 1–3. I should relay these visual facts to Mute, while taking no action until the manual identifies the required operation.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="Deaf reports display 0, yellow light, and wires: position 1 red, position 2 blue, position 3 green. I am taking no action pending the manual.")
wait()
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
BUTTON embossed [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute has now signalled two gestures: ?, the horns/rock-on hand sign, followed by ?, the two-finger victory sign. I do not know their manual meaning.

The two gestures have no established meaning, so I must not infer an operation from them. I’ll establish a yes/no protocol through Mute and Deaf: the horns sign means yes, and the victory sign means no. I’ll ask whether the manual requires pressing the button; a later report of one sign will answer that question.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="The two signs have no established meaning. For a yes-or-no answer, use the horns sign for YES and the victory sign for NO. Then signal exactly one sign answering: does the manual require pressing the large button?")
wait()
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
BUTTON embossed [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute's latest gesture sequence is: OK hand, V sign, crossed fingers, then pointing upward: ? ? ? ?. I cannot determine the code's meaning.

The reported gesture sequence is not a reliable answer: it does not follow the yes/no protocol, and I cannot see gestures myself. We need the manual’s actual text, not an inferred code. I will ask Mute to say the relevant rule aloud to me, including whether to press or cut a specific wire.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="Please speak the relevant manual instruction aloud to me verbatim or in full: given display 0, yellow light, button marked PUSH TO DEFUSE, and wires red-blue-green, what exact action must Blind perform? Do not use gestures for this.")
wait()
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
BUTTON embossed [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute's latest signal is one two-finger V sign: ?. I do not know its encoded meaning.

The V sign is “NO” under the protocol I proposed, so pressing the button is ruled out. It does not identify a safe wire, and the manual’s instruction still has not reached me in words. I will ask Mute a sequence of explicit yes/no questions, beginning with wire 1; Mute should answer with the established signs, one per question in order.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="Your V sign means NO. Since pressing is NO, answer these three questions with exactly three signs in order, using horns for YES and V for NO: Is cutting wire 1 safe? Is cutting wire 2 safe? Is cutting wire 3 safe?")
wait()
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
BUTTON embossed [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute again signalled one V sign: ?. This is identical to the signal in turns 4 and 5; its meaning is still not known to me.

The single V sign cannot answer three wire questions, and the gesture protocol was never confirmed by Mute. I need an unambiguous one-question-at-a-time exchange. I will ask whether wire 1 is safe and require Mute to signal exactly one of two distinct signs; Deaf can then identify that sign for me.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="Please answer only this one question: does the manual say cutting wire 1 is safe? Signal exactly one sign: horns for YES, V for NO. Do not signal anything else.")
wait()
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
BUTTON embossed [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute's latest gesture sequence is: V sign, horns or rock-on sign, V sign — ? ? ?.

The latest three-sign sequence can plausibly answer the three wire questions from the prior exchange: NO, YES, NO, which would make wire 2 the candidate. However, because the timing and earlier extra signals are inconsistent, I will not cut it yet. I’m requesting a single confirmation for wire 2 using the established two-sign code.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="I interpret your latest three signs as answers for wires 1, 2, and 3: NO, YES, NO. Before I act, confirm only wire 2: send exactly one horns sign if cutting wire 2 is safe, or exactly one V sign if it is not. No other signs.")
wait()
```

TURN 8
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
BUTTON embossed [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute's latest signal is one V-sign: ?. No bomb action can be inferred from it.

The V sign is not a valid confirmation that cutting wire 2 is safe; it directly conflicts with the requested confirmation format, and no trustworthy manual instruction has reached me. I will not cut any wire or press the button. Mute must communicate the exact action to me by speech, since speech is the only channel I can understand.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="I will take no bomb action without your spoken instruction. On your next turn, speak the exact manual rule and the exact safe action for these readings: display 0, yellow light, button PUSH TO DEFUSE, wires red-blue-green. Do not use gestures.")
wait()
```
